coordinates.note: REVIEW REQUIRED (A17), after real effort: no official KEK, SuperKEKB or Belle II page, and no technical paper (including the Belle II TDR abstract and the Belle NIM detector paper) reached in this session, publishes latitude/longitude for the Tsukuba interaction region; en.wikipedia's own infobox coordinate for Belle II carries no citation for its number either. The numeric value is inherited from that uncited Wikipedia coordinate (kept as src:belle2-wikipedia-coordinates in the record's top-level sources for provenance); it is not cited on this coordinate because A17 rejects a rank-12 source as the sole backing for a `detector`-kind point. KEK's own SuperKEKB site gives only the postal address (1-1 Oho, Tsukuba, Ibaraki 305-0801), confirming the campus but not a precise point. precision_m widened from 300 to 400 m to reflect that this is an unsurveyed estimate.

name: KEK Tsukuba interaction region (Belle II)
notes: Depth below the surface is not recorded: the SuperKEKB ring is commonly described as roughly 11 m underground, but no source fetched in this session states this on an official page, so the field is left null.

summary.plain: The collision hall on the KEK laboratory campus in Tsukuba, Japan, where the electron and positron beams of the KEKB and SuperKEKB rings are brought together and where the Belle and Belle II detectors have stood.
summary.technical: The Tsukuba straight section of the KEKB/SuperKEKB double-ring collider, housing the interaction point and final-focus system; home of the Belle detector (1999-2010) and, after the roll-in of 11 April 2017, of Belle II.
